Scriptable.Summary: Calculates desired motion via a custom function provided through SetDragStyleFunction().

TranslateLine.Summary: 1D motion along the detector's Axis, by default the world Y axis.

TranslateLineOrPlane.Summary: 1D motion along the detector's Axis and, when the modifier is active, 2D motion in the plane perpendicular to the detector's Axis.

TranslatePlane.Summary: 2D motion in the plane perpendicular to the detector's Axis, by default the world XZ plane.

TranslatePlaneOrLine.Summary: 2D motion in the plane perpendicular to the detector's Axis and, when the modifier is active, 1D motion along the detector's Axis.

TranslateViewPlane.Summary: 2D motion in the plane perpendicular to the camera's view. In this mode, the plane is constantly updated, even while dragging, and will always face the camera's current view.

Scriptable.Summary: Invokes the function registered via DragDetector:SetPermissionPolicyFunction(), enabling/disabling the detector based on whether the function returns true or false.

Custom.Summary: The object will not move at all, but DragFrame will still be updated and you can respond to drag manipulation however you'd like.

Geometric.Summary: For an Anchored object both inside the running experience and in Studio edit mode, the position/orientation of the object will be updated to exactly reflect the proposed motion. For an unanchored object, behavior is the same as for an anchored object; however, in a running experience, the object will be anchored at the start of the drag and restored to unanchored upon drag release.

Physical.Summary: An Anchored object will default to Geometric behavior as it is not affected by forces. An unanchored object will be moved by constraint forces that attempt to bring it to the desired position and/or orientation given by the proposed motion.

In.Summary: The easing style is applied in a forward direction.

InOut.Summary: The easing style is applied forward for the first half and in reverse for the second half.

Out.Summary: The easing style is applied in a reverse direction.

Back.Summary: Slightly overshoots the target, then backs into place.

Bounce.Summary: Bounces backwards multiple times after reaching the target, before eventually settling.

Circular.Summary: Follows a circular arc, such that acceleration is more sudden and deceleration more gradual versus Quint or Exponential.

Cubic.Summary: Similar to Quad but with a slightly sharper curve based on cubic interpolation.

Elastic.Summary: Moves as if attached to a rubber band, overshooting the target several times.

Exponential.Summary: The sharpest curve based on exponential interpolation.

Quad.Summary: Similar to Sine but with a slightly sharper curve based on quadratic interpolation.

Quart.Summary: Similar to Cubic but with an even sharper curve based on quartic interpolation.

Quint.Summary: Similar to Quart but with an even sharper curve based on quintic interpolation.

Sine.Summary: Speed is determined by a sine wave for a gentle easing motion.

Always.Summary: Scrolling is always elastic, even when there isn't content available to scroll to.

Never.Summary: Scrolling is never elastic and the canvas will never scroll beyond its bounds.

WhenScrollable.Summary: Scrolling is elastic when there is content to be scrolled to.

Append.Summary: Commits the recorded work and merges with the previous recording if possible.

Cancel.Summary: Cancels the recording, automatically undoing any work in progress.

Automatic.Summary: Let the physics engine select the geometric representation for aerodynamic force and torque calculations.

UseCollisionGeometry.Summary: Use the current collision geometry specified by TriangleMeshPart.CollisionFidelity for aerodynamic force and torque calculations .

UsePreciseGeometry.Summary: Force the engine to compute aerodynamic forces and torques using a more precise geometry representation based on the original mesh. This option may increase join and replication time if used on a large scale.

Default.Summary: Aerodynamic forces will not be calculated on any BaseParts.

Experimental.Summary: Aerodynamic forces will be calculated on BaseParts with EnableFluidForces set to true. During the beta phase, the behavior of the aerodynamic force model may change as the model improves.

Arial.Summary: Arial has been removed from Roblox. Using Arial will map to Arimo.

ArialBold.Summary: Arial has been removed from Roblox. Using Arial will map to Arimo.

Gotham.Summary: Gotham has been removed from Roblox. Using Gotham will map to Montserrat.

GothamBlack.Summary: Gotham has been removed from Roblox. Using Gotham will map to Montserrat.

GothamBold.Summary: Gotham has been removed from Roblox. Using Gotham will map to Montserrat.

GothamMedium.Summary: Gotham has been removed from Roblox. Using Gotham will map to Montserrat.

Unknown.Summary: Set when the TextLabel.FontFace property is set to a Font that has no corresponding enum value.

Italic.Summary: The text renders italic with this font.

Normal.Summary: The text renders normally with this font.

Magnitude.Summary: A single number is used to specify the magnitude of the maximum constraint force. The constraint will ensure that the force it applies will have a magnitude that is less than this limit.

PerAxis.Summary: A vector is used to specify the maximum force value along each axis of a given reference frame. The constraint will ensure that each component of the force will have an absolute value that's less than the corresponding vector entry.

Brick.Summary: Increases by a rate of 1 along the x- and z- axes, 1.2 along the y-axis.

Custom.Summary: Increases by a rate as low as .001 along all axes.

Plate.Summary: Increases by a rate of 1 along the x- and z- axes, 0.4 along the y-axis.

Symmetric.Summary: Increases by a rate of 1 along all axes.

ChatBlue.Summary: Causes the frame to appear similar to a Dialog with its Tone property set to DialogTone.Neutral. Like ChatGreen and ChatRed, this has a padding of fifteen pixels on all sides.

ChatGreen.Summary: Causes the frame to appear similar to a Dialog with its Tone property set to DialogTone.Friendly. Like ChatBlue and ChatRed, this has a padding of fifteen pixels on all sides.

ChatRed.Summary: Causes the frame to appear similar to a Dialog with its Tone property set to DialogTone.Enemy. Like ChatBlue and ChatGreen, this has a padding of fifteen pixels on all sides.

Custom.Summary: Uses the frame's GuiObject.BackgroundColor3, GuiObject.BorderColor3, and GuiObject.BackgroundTransparency properties to determine the frame's appearance. It has no padding; elements with the position UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0) will appear at the frame's top-left corner.

DropShadow.Summary: Causes the frame to appear as a translucent gray rectangle with blurred sides. The blur is more apparent on the bottom edge. It has a padding of eight pixels on all sides.

RobloxRound.Summary: Causes the frame to appear as a translucent dark gray rectangle with rounded edges. Like RobloxSquare, this has a padding of five pixels on all sides.

RobloxSquare.Summary: Causes the frame to appear as a translucent dark gray rectangle with a padding of five pixels on all sides.

Revoke.Summary: A player revokes (cancels) a previously invoked (sent) connection request.

FriendRequestReceived.Summary: At least one of two players has received a connection request sent by the other player.

FriendRequestSent.Summary: At least one of two players has sent a connection request to the other player.

Unknown.Summary: The connection status of two players is unknown.

PlayerChoice.Summary: The rig (either R6 or R15) determined by a player's character settings set on the website in the 'Edit Avatar' page.

MatchingGenreOnly.Summary: Only gear genres matching the allowed genres specified in a place's configuration settings.

Adventure.Summary: The game's genre is set to Adventure.

All.Summary: The game's genre is set to All. The game will be listed as all possible genres.

Fantasy.Summary: The game's genre is set to Fantasy.

Funny.Summary: The game's genre is set to Funny.

Ninja.Summary: The game's genre is set to Ninja.

Pirate.Summary: The game's genre is set to Pirate.

Scary.Summary: The game's genre is set to Scary.

SciFi.Summary: The game's genre is set to SciFi (Science Fiction).

SkatePark.Summary: The game's genre is set to Skate Park.

Sports.Summary: The game's genre is set to Sports.

TownAndCity.Summary: The game's genre is set to Town and City.

Tutorial.Summary: The game's genre is set to Tutorial.

War.Summary: The game's genre is set to War.

WildWest.Summary: The game's genre is set to Wild West.

Automatic.Summary: Roblox will automatically decide what graphics mode to use, depending on what best suits your device's specifications.

NoGraphics.Summary: Game will not be rendered, and instead a Diagnostics window is rendered on screen.

Hover.Summary: The GUI is being hovered over by the user.

NonInteractable.Summary: The GUI cannot be interacted with and therefore has no states.

Press.Summary: The GUI is being pressed/held down by the user.

Custom.Summary: Allows for application of a custom haptic waveform through the HapticEffect:SetWaveformKeys() method.

GameplayCollision.Summary: This effect is a large immediate rumble that dies down quickly, useful to signify a clear and purposeful impact between objects.

GameplayExplosion.Summary: Useful to signify a large-scale physics event that triggers impact across a large portion of a given scene. This effect is high intensity in order to represent the magnitude of the impact and it lingers for a longer period of time than GameplayCollision.

UIClick.Summary: Useful for when a player has selected an object (often a UI object) with the intention of triggering its action. This effect type is crisp and it provides immediate feedback without being overwhelming.

UIHover.Summary: Useful for when a player browses over an object (often a UI object) without the intention of triggering its action; it can also alert the player that they have browsed over an interactable object. This effect type is subtle and does not disrupt the gameplay experience.

UINotification.Summary: Useful for when there is an inbound message that should draw the player's attention away from their current gameplay and prompt them that the notification requires immediate attention or action.

AlwaysOnTop.Summary: Allows the Highlight to display regardless if there are objects between the camera and the highlighted object. This means the viewer is always able to see the highlight regardless of what is between the highlighted object and the camera.

Occluded.Summary: Hides the Highlight if there are objects between the camera and the highlighted object. This means the viewer is only able to see the object if there are no obstructing objects between the highlighted object and the camera's view.

Center.Summary: Grid is aligned to the center of its parent along the X axis.

Left.Summary: Grid is aligned to the left edge of its parent.

Right.Summary: Grid is aligned to the right edge of its parent.

InnerBox.Summary: Fixed size collision boxes, similar to the classic avatar collision.

OuterBox.Summary: Dynamically sized collision boxes based on mesh sizes.

None.Summary: A player selecting None on their Humanoid will not have their Name and healthbar displayed to other players under any circumstance (this can be thought of as the highest priority).

Subject.Summary: A player selecting Subject on their Humanoid will allow other players to see their Name and healthbar if those other players are within the distance settings set in the Humanoid selecting Subject (this can be thought of as the second highest priority).

Viewer.Summary: A player selecting Viewer on their Humanoid will see the Name and healthbar of other players if those other players are within the distance settings set in the Humanoid selecting Viewer (this can be thought of as the lowest priority, and will not be taken into account if other players are selecting 'Subject' or 'None').

AlwaysOff.Summary: The humanoid's health bar is never visible.

AlwaysOn.Summary: The humanoid's health bar is always visible (assuming MaxHealth is greater than zero).

DisplayWhenDamaged.Summary: The humanoid's health bar is only visible when the humanoid is not at full health (assuming MaxHealth is greater than zero).

R15.Summary: Indicates that a character is using the new R15 rig.

R6.Summary: Indicates that a character is using the legacy R6 rig.

Climbing.Summary: The Humanoid is climbing (e.g. up a TrussPart or ladder).

Dead.Summary: The Humanoid died. Changing a Humanoid's state to this state will kill it.

FallingDown.Summary: The Humanoid has been tripped, and will attempt to get up in a few moments.

Flying.Summary: When set, the Humanoid won't be animated, as with the Humanoid.PlatformStand property. This state lasts as long as the player flies.

Freefall.Summary: The Humanoid is currently freefalling (jumped from a height or fell off a ledge).

GettingUp.Summary: The Humanoid is getting back on their feet after FallingDown or Ragdoll.

Jumping.Summary: The Humanoid just jumped. (Check Humanoid.Jump). This state lasts only briefly. This state normally transitions into either Landed, if on the ground, or Freefall, if still in the air.

Landed.Summary: The Humanoid touched the ground after a Freefall. This state lasts only briefly.

None.Summary: Unusable placeholder in case an unknown state gets triggered internally.

Physics.Summary: The Humanoid doesn't apply any force on its own and will not automatically transition to any other state. This state has to be set and unset manually using Humanoid:ChangeState().

PlatformStanding.Summary: The Humanoid is platformstanding. Check the Humanoid.PlatformStand property.

Ragdoll.Summary: (Deprecated) The Humanoid has been hit by a fast moving object (uncontrolled falling). The Humanoid can recover from this. This state has to be set and unset manually using Humanoid:ChangeState().

RunningNoPhysics.Summary: (Deprecated) Currently running and not near other physical objects.

Seated.Summary: The Humanoid is currently sitting in a Seat or VehicleSeat. Check the Humanoid.Sit property.

StrafingNoPhysics.Summary: Not currently used with default Humanoid. Cannot be set with Humanoid:ChangeState().

Swimming.Summary: The Humanoid is currently swimming in Terrain water.

IncludeContactedMechanisms.Summary: The part, any parts directly joined to it via joints/constraints, and any parts which it comes into contact with during the solve will be moved during the resolution. That is, the moved parts will be allowed to "push" other unanchored parts in the workspace out of the way in order to get to the target position.

NoCollisions.Summary: Only the part and any parts directly joined to it via joints/constraints be involved in the resolution, everything else in the workspace will be treated as though it doesn't exist.

OtherMechanismsAnchored.Summary: Only the part and any parts directly jointed to it via joints/constraints will be moved during resolution, but they will collide with other objects in the workspace.

Default.Summary: The default option for IKControls. The default is currently set to Enabled.

Disabled.Summary: Disables support for constraints for IKControls. When disabled, IKControls still work, but ignore physics constraints.

Enabled.Summary: Enables support for constraints for IKControls.

LookAt.Summary: Moves and orients the whole chain to make the forward axis on the EndEffector point at a position in the world specified by Target.

Position.Summary: Aligns the EndEffector position to that of the Target .

Rotation.Summary: Aligns the EndEffector rotation to that of the Target.

Transform.Summary: It is a full 6-DoF constraint. Aligns the EndEffector CFrame to that of the Target. It is the default value.

Default.Summary: The default behavior in which neither color nor alpha values are locked.

LockCanvasAlpha.Summary: The alpha values of the image will not be modified.

LockCanvasColor.Summary: The color values of the image will not be modified.

Add.Summary: Adds pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together.

AlphaBlend.Summary: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination based on the alpha of the source pixels. Unlike BlendSourceOver, the destination color in AlphaBlend affects the resulting color of the image, regardless of the destination color's alpha.

BlendSourceOver.Summary: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination using source over alpha blending.

Multiply.Summary: Multiplies pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together. RGBA values are multiplied as values between 0 and 1. Values lower than 1 have a darkening effect on the image.

Overwrite.Summary: Overwrites all pixels in the destination image with pixels from the source image.

Center.Summary: The object's location is centered on it's parent.

Edge.Summary: The object is located along an edge of its parent.

Inset.Summary: The object's located is inset from its parent's location.

Bottom.Summary: The widget will appear docked below the game screen.

Float.Summary: The widget will not be docked to any side of the game screen, and instead can be freely dragged around.

Left.Summary: The widget will appear docked to the left of the game screen.

Right.Summary: The widget will appear docked to the right of the game screen.

Top.Summary: The widget will appear docked above the game screen.

Bool.Summary: The InputAction will receive boolean values from button inputs, for example true/false on press/release from inputs such as KeyCode.ButtonA or KeyCode.E. This setting also exposes the UIButton property on child InputBindings, allowing you to easily hook up press or release of a GuiButton for the action.

Direction1D.Summary: The InputAction will receive numerical values, generally from analog gamepad triggers such as KeyCode.ButtonL2 or KeyCode.ButtonR2. This setting also exposes the Up and Down properties on child InputBindings, allowing for boolean inputs or "1D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

Direction2D.Summary: The InputAction will receive Vector2 values, generally from thumbstick inputs such as KeyCode.Thumbstick1 and KeyCode.Thumbstick2. This setting also exposes the Up, Down, Left, and Right properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "2D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

Direction3D.Summary: The InputAction will receive Vector3 values from inputs assigned to the Up, Down, Left, Right, Forward, and/or Backward properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "3D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

NoInput.Summary: Behaves like a weld and does nothing.

Sin.Summary: Rotate at a velocity of: ParamA * math.sin(workspace.DistributedGameTime * ParamB), where BasePart ParamA determines the maximum speed at which the part spins, and BasePart ParamB determines how frequently it changes direction.

Automatic.Summary: Aligns the siblings of the UIListLayout or the specific UIFlexItem parent to the layout's HorizontalAlignment or VerticalAlignment, depending on its FillDirection. If HorizontalFlex or VerticalFlex is enabled for the UIListLayout cross‑direction, Stretch will be used for that direction.

Center.Summary: Aligns the siblings of the UIListLayout or the specific UIFlexItem parent to the line's center in either a horizontal or vertical fill.

End.Summary: Aligns the siblings of the UIListLayout or the specific UIFlexItem parent to the line's bottom in a horizontal fill or the line's right in a vertical fill.

Start.Summary: Aligns the siblings of the UIListLayout or the specific UIFlexItem parent to the line's top in a horizontal fill or the line's left in a vertical fill.

Stretch.Summary: Stretches the siblings of the UIListLayout or the specific UIFlexItem parent to fill the entire cross‑direction of the line in either a horizontal or vertical fill.

All.Summary: Joints are created between any kind of surface. Functions identically to Surface.

None.Summary: Joints are never created, no matter what.

Surface.Summary: Joints are created between any kind of surface. Functions identically to All.

Euro.Summary: The € key. Only present on certain keyboards.

F13.Summary: The F13 key. Only present on certain keyboards.

F14.Summary: The F14 key. Only present on certain keyboards.

F15.Summary: The F15 key. Only present on certain keyboards.

LeftSuper.Summary: The left side Super key. Better known as the Windows key or Cmd key.

MouseBackButton.DeprecationMessage: This enum is deprecated and flagged for removal.

MouseNoButton.DeprecationMessage: This enum is deprecated and flagged for removal.

MouseX.DeprecationMessage: This enum is deprecated and flagged for removal.

MouseY.DeprecationMessage: This enum is deprecated and flagged for removal.

NumLock.Summary: The Num Lock key on the keypad cluster.

RightSuper.Summary: The right side Super key. Better known as the Windows key or Cmd key.

Unknown.Summary: Blank value that represents no key being pressed.

Constant.Summary: The segment starting at this key will constantly evaluate to the value set at this key.

Cubic.Summary: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using cubic interpolation of this key value using its right tangent and the next key value and its left tangent.

Linear.Summary: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using a linear interpolation at this key and the value at the next key.

Center.Summary: The object is centered on the center of its parent (X axis), expanding equally to the left and right of the parent's center.

Left.Summary: The object is on the left side of its parent (X axis).

Right.Summary: The object is on the right side of its parent (X axis).

Realistic.Summary: The most advanced and realistic lighting and shadows Roblox can deliver.

Soft.Summary: A flat, retro-Roblox look with softer lights and shadows.

Head.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Head.

LeftArm.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Left Arm. This includes UpperLeftArm, LowerLeftArm, and LeftHand for R15 rigs.

LeftLeg.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Left Leg. This includes UpperLeftLeg, LowerLeftLeg and LeftFoot for R15 rigs.

RightArm.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Right Arm. This includes UpperRightArm, LowerRightArm and RightHand for R15 rigs.

RightLeg.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Right Leg. This includes UpperRightLeg, LowerRightLeg, and RightFoot for R15 rigs.

Torso.Summary: If the limb is a part of the Humanoid's Torso. This includes UpperTorso and LowerTorso for R15 rigs.

Unknown.Summary: If a part is not a limb (e.g. running the Humanoid:GetLimb() function and passing it an accessory which is a sibling of the Humanoid will return this value).

Camera.Summary:
All of the following, resulting in the world being heard from the perspective (postition and orientation) of the camera.

  • An AudioListener will be created and parented to Workspace.CurrentCamera.
  • An AudioDeviceOutput will be created and parented to SoundService.
  • A Wire will be created and parented to the previously-created AudioListener. The wire's SourceInstance will be set to the previously-created AudioListener and its TargetInstance will be set to the previously-created AudioDeviceOutput.

Character.Summary:
All of the following, resulting in the world being heard from the position of your character while matching the orientation of your camera.

  • An Attachment will be created and parented to the PrimaryPart of the local player's Character model.

  • An AudioListener will be created and parented to the Attachment.

  • An AudioDeviceOutput will be created and parented to SoundService.

  • A Wire will be created and parented to the previously-created AudioListener. The wire's SourceInstance will be set to the previously-created AudioListener and its TargetInstance will be set to the previously-created AudioDeviceOutput.

  • The previously-created Attachment will be updated once per frame to face the same direction as Workspace.CurrentCamera.

Default.Summary: Behavior depends on the value of VoiceChatService.EnableDefaultVoice and VoiceChatService.UseAudioApi. When using the default voice setup with the audio API, this behaves similarly to Camera.

None.Summary: No AudioListener will be created by default, but they can be created separately by scripts.

ObjectCFrame.Summary: Uses the world CFrame from an instance.

ObjectPosition.Summary: Uses the world position of an instance and the rotation of workspace.CurrentCamera.

Default.Summary: The behavior of the default setting is not constant. It can mean Disabled or Enabled depending on what the global back-end flag settings are currently.

Disabled.Summary: This means layered clothing will not be equipped on characters in the experience.

Enabled.Summary: This means layered clothing will be equipped on characters in the experience (Although MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories also need to be enabled for the experience).

Completed.Summary: User confirmed the purchase and the transaction has been processed.

Error.Summary: User confirmed the purchase, but the transaction cannot be sent to the backend for processing.

AlreadyOwned.Summary: Unable to purchase item because user already owns the item. Users can only own one copy of non-limited item.

InsufficientMembership.Summary: The user does not have sufficient premium membership to purchase this item.

InsufficientRobux.Summary: Unable to purchase item because of insufficient Robux.

NotAvailableForPurchaser.Summary: This item is restricted to a group of users and the purchaser is not in this group.

PlaceInvalid.Summary: The item is not allowed to be sold in the place.

PriceMismatch.Summary: The provided price does not match the item price. Most likely the price changed since displayed to the user.

PurchaserIsSeller.Summary: The purchaser is the same user as the seller, for a resale purchase.

QuantityLimitExceeded.Summary: User has reached the max quantity allowed per user set by the creator for limited items.

QuotaExceeded.Summary: The user has exceeded our purchase request limit.

SystemError.Summary: Unable to purchase item due to Roblox system error.

Default.Summary: Includes desktop, mobile, cross-play enabled players, etc.

ForceField.Summary: Must be used on a MeshPart with UVs laid out to cover much of the 0:1 UV space or more (larger is better). The MeshPart must also have a texture applied to its TextureID, and that texture image must have a wide value range since the material displays the range from dark/black to light/white values. Obtain this model for a functional example.

Glass.Summary: Applies to BasePart only. Note that refraction of light through this material is not supported on mobile devices due to computational limitations.

Organic.Summary: Material pattern has less repetition, like stone or dirt.

Regular.Summary: Material has ordered pattern, usually man-made, like brick or wood planks.

None.Summary: The player does not have an active paid membership.

Premium.Summary: The player has an active Premium membership.

DistanceBased.Summary: Select level of detail based on distance (default behavior as in game).

Default.Summary: The default option to control the Workspace.MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories feature. This currently has the same meaning as "Enabled".

Enabled.Summary: Enables the Workspace.MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories feature.

Brick.Summary: The mesh is a brick (just like the shape of a default BasePart).

FileMesh.Summary: The mesh is determined by the Roblox mesh asset ID provided.

Head.Summary: The mesh is the default Humanoid head mesh.

RightAngleRamp.Summary: The mesh is a right angle ramp.

Torso.Summary: The mesh is the default Humanoid torso mesh.

MessageError.Summary: The message is from the error channel.

MessageInfo.Summary: The message is from the information channel.

MessageOutput.Summary: The message is from the standard output channel.

MessageWarning.Summary: The message is from the warning channel.

Disabled.Summary: A lower resolution mesh will not be displayed.

StreamingMesh.Summary: A lower resolution "imposter" mesh (colored, coarse mesh that wraps around all child parts of the model) renders outside the streaming radius.

Default.Summary: Engine determines best behavior. Currently equivalent to Legacy.

Improved.Summary: Models are never sent during player join. Models that are "non-spatial" (containing no BasePart descendants) are sent soon after join, but before the Workspace.PersistentLoaded event fires. Models that are "spatial" (containing BasePart descendants) are sent when any BasePart descendant needs to be streamed to a client, and may stream out when all BasePart descendants are eligible to stream out.

Legacy.Summary: Models are sent when their parent is sent, typically during player join. Models are never streamed out unless an ancestor of the model is streamed out.

Atomic.Summary: The Model and all of its descendants are streamed in/out together. For streaming in, this applies when any descendant BasePart is eligible for streaming in. For streaming out, this applies when all descendant BaseParts are eligible for streaming out.

Default.Summary: Engine determines best behavior. Currently equivalent to Nonatomic.

Nonatomic.Summary: When a nonatomic model is streamed, descendants are also sent, except for part descendants. Nonatomic models that are not descendants of parts are sent during experience loading.

Persistent.Summary: Persistent models are sent as a complete atomic unit soon after the player joins and before the Workspace.PersistentLoaded event fires. Persistent models and their descendants are never streamed out.

PersistentPerPlayer.Summary: Behaves as a persistent model for players that have been added using Model:AddPersistentPlayer(). For other players, behavior is the same as Atomic. You can revert a model from player persistence via Model:RemovePersistentPlayer().

Default.Summary: The mouse moves freely around the user's screen.

LockCenter.Summary: The mouse is locked and cannot move from the center of the user's screen.

LockCurrentPosition.Summary: The mouse is locked and cannot move from its current position on the user's screen at the time of locking.

Coasting.Summary: Skateboard is coasting (not actively speeding up / being pushed).

Default.Summary: The default option for Workspace.MoverConstraintRootBehavior. Currently set to Disabled.

Disabled.Summary: The legacy logic will be used for assembly root part selection when a mechanism contains a mover constraint.

Enabled.Summary: Improved logic will be used for assembly root part selection when a mechanism contains a mover constraint. This improved logic gives more consistent behavior when compared with other constraints or the deprecated BodyMover classes.

Automatic.Summary: Network ownership is determined automatically by the server.

Manual.Summary: Network ownership is set manually by the developer.

OnContact.Summary: The first player to touch a part is given ownership of that part for the server (network). Ownership will not change if another player touches that part unless network ownership has been released by the owner.

ForceHide.Summary: The mouse icon is forced to always remain hidden/invisible.

ForceShow.Summary: The mouse icon is forced to always remain shown/visible.

None.Summary: The mouse icon behavior is not overridden - default behavior is used.

Edit.Summary: The current user or group roleset can download a copy of the package from Roblox and publish package changes to Roblox.

NoAccess.Summary: The current user or group roleset doesn't have access.

None.Summary: Permission data is not available for the current user or group roleset.

Own.Summary: The current user or group roleset can download a copy of the page from Roblox, publish package changes to Roblox, and manage who has access to the package.

Revoked.Summary: The current user's or group roleset's permission is revoked.

UseView.Summary: The current user or group roleset can download a copy of the package from Roblox.

CornerWedge.Summary: A wedge shape with slopes on two sides.

Cylinder.Summary: A cylinder shape oriented along the X axis.

Wedge.Summary: A wedge shape with a slope on one side.

None.Summary: Disable flipbook features and use the texture as a single static texture over the particle's lifetime.

Loop.Summary: Continuously play through all frames, starting back at the first frame after playing the last.

OneShot.Summary: Play through the animation only once across the particle's lifetime. With this setting, the ParticleEmitter.FlipbookFramerate property doesn't apply; instead, the framerate is determined by the particle's ParticleEmitter.Lifetime divided evenly by the number of frames in the animation. OneShot animations are useful for clear non-repeating animations, such as an explosion that creates a puff of smoke and then fades out.

PingPong.Summary: Play from the first to the last frame, then in reverse from the last to the first, repeating throughout the ParticleEmitter.Lifetime of the particle.

Random.Summary: Play the frames in a random order, blending/crossfading from one frame to the next. This can be useful for organic particle textures at low framerates, such as stars slowly twinkling between subtly different shapes.

ClosestNoPath.Summary: Path doesn't exist, returns path to closest point.

ClosestOutOfRange.Summary: Goal is out of MaxDistance range, returns path to closest point you can reach within MaxDistance.

FailFinishNotEmpty.Summary: Failed to compute path; the finish point is not empty.

FailStartNotEmpty.Summary: Failed to compute path; the starting point is not empty.

Jump.Summary: Jump action needed to reach the next waypoint.

Walk.Summary: Walk action needed to reach the next waypoint.

Game.Summary: Member must have no security permissions in order to be shown.

Roblox.Summary: Member is shown no matter what security it has.

Studio.Summary: Member must have security permissions less than or equal to LocalUserSecurity to be shown.

Adaptive.Summary: The engine attempts to assign optimal simulation rates for individual assemblies of either 240 Hz, 120 Hz, or 60 Hz. This setting is optimized for performance.

Default.Summary: The current default is Fixed.

Fixed.Summary: All simulated assemblies inside the workspace will advance forward at 240 Hz. This option is best for optimal stability and simulation accuracy.

Android.Summary: The client is running on Android (Google mobile).

AndroidTV.Summary: The client is running on an Android TV.

IOS.Summary: The client is running on IOS (Apple mobile).

Linux.Summary: The client is running on a Linux Operating System (desktop).

NX.Summary: The client is running on an NX Operating System (Cisco Nexus).

None.Summary: The client's operating system is unknown.

OSX.Summary: The client is running on OSX (Apple desktop).

Ouya.Summary: The client is running on an Ouya Operating System (Android-Based).

PS3.Summary: The client is running on a PS3 (console).

PS4.Summary: The client is running on a PS4 (console).

WiiU.Summary: The client is running on a Wii U (console).

Windows.Summary: The client is running on a Windows Operating System.

XBox360.Summary: The client is running on an XBox 360 (console).

XBoxOne.Summary: The client is running on an XBox One (console).

Begin.Summary: The tween has been created, but has yet to be played. After exiting this state, the tween never enters it again.

Delayed.Summary: The tween is waiting for the duration specified in its TweenInfo.DelayTime. After the delay elapses, the tween plays.

Paused.Summary: The tween is paused in the middle of playing.

All.Summary: A global message that everyone can receive.

Team.Summary: A team message only players in the same team can receive.

Whisper.Summary: A whispered message only the person it's whispered to can receive.

In.Summary: The EasingStyle curve is reversed, with the easing becoming linear as it approaches the next keyframe.

InOut.Summary: Two easing curves are applied back-to-back with the linear ends of the curves meeting in the middle.

Out.Summary: EasingStyle curves are applied in the forward direction, from the current keyframe to the next.

Bounce.Summary: Pose interpolation produces a bounce like effect between key frames.

Constant.Summary: Poses do not interpolate but snap to the key frame indicated by the PoseEasingDirection.

Cubic.Summary: Deprecated - Use PoseEasingStyle.CubicV2. Pose interpolation is a cubic curve between keyframes based on the PoseEasingDirection.
Cubic.DeprecationMessage: Use CubicV2 going forward, Cubic has a bug where the direction is reversed between the editor and runtime.

CubicV2.Summary: Pose interpolation is a cubic curve between keyframes based on PoseEasingDirection.

Elastic.Summary: Pose interpolation will overshoot like it is elastic.

Gamepad.Summary: The player has connected or most recently interacted with a gamepad.

KeyboardAndMouse.Summary: The player has connected or most recently interacted with a keyboard or mouse.

Touch.Summary: The player's device has touch capability and no other input method is available or connected.

AllGames.Summary: (Default) Item is purchasable in the Marketplace and all experiences.

AllowedGames.Summary: Item is purchasable in the Marketplace and experiences owned by the item creator.

AvatarShop.Summary: Item is purchasable only in the Marketplace.

AdReward.Summary: The product was rewarded to the user when they watched a video ad to completion.

CommerceProduct.Summary: The user acquired the product as a benefit of purchasing commerce merchandise from the developer of the experience.

ExperienceDetailsPage.Summary: The purchase was made outside of an experience, on the Store tab of the experience details page.

InExperience.Summary: The purchase was made inside of an experience.

NotProcessedYet.Summary: The purchase request has been sent but not yet processed.

PurchaseGranted.Summary: The purchase has been processed and granted to the user who initiated the purchase request.

AlwaysShow.Summary: This prompt will always show when in range and visible.

OneGlobally.Summary: Only one prompt will be shown with this setting.

OnePerButton.Summary: One prompt will be shown per input KeyCode.

Custom.Summary: Custom prompt UI style as set by the developer. For more information, see ProximityPrompt.Style.

Default.Summary: The default prompt UI style.

Automatic.Summary: The quality level of graphics is determined automatically depending on the client's setting for either game performance or graphic quality.

Level01.Summary: Graphic quality level 1 - the lowest quality level.

Level21.Summary: Graphic quality level 21, the highest quality level.

InnerBox.Summary: Fixed size collision boxes, similar to the classic avatar collision.

OuterBox.Summary: Dynamically sized collision boxes based on mesh sizes.

Exclude.Summary: Every BasePart in the raycast operation will be considered except those that are descendants of objects in the filter list.

Include.Summary: Only BaseParts which are descendants of objects in the filter list will be considered in the raycast operation.

Automatic.Summary: Object's level of detail is dynamically controlled by its distance from the camera (see table above).

Performance.Summary: Push performance as much as possible, trying to maintain quality if possible, and discarding appearance if that's necessary to reach performance. This means that the performance will always be excellent, but mesh visuals may be affected negatively.

Precise.Summary: Object is rendered in the highest fidelity regardless of its distance from the camera.

Last.Summary: This should run as last, after Character.

Default.Summary: Bilinear filtering of the four near pixels in the image.

Pixelated.Summary: Nearest neighbor filtering of the closest pixel in the image.

Alley.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in an alley.

Arena.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in an arena.

Auditorium.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in an auditorium.

Bathroom.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a bathroom.

CarpettedHallway.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a carpeted hallway.

Cave.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a cave.

City.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a city.

ConcertHall.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a concert hall.

Forest.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a forest.

GenericReverb.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to a generic reverb effect.

Hallway.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a hallway.

Hangar.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a hangar.

LivingRoom.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a living room.

Mountains.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in the mountains.

NoReverb.Summary: No sound reverb. Audio is not changed from default.

PaddedCell.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a padded cell.

ParkingLot.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a parking lot.

Plain.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is an open plain.

Quarry.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a quarry.

Room.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a room.

SewerPipe.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a sewer pipe.

StoneCorridor.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a stone corridor.

StoneRoom.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is in a stone room.

UnderWater.Summary: Sound reverb is changed to sound like the player is underwater.

MaterialPicker.Summary: Deprecated in favor of Material Manager. Don't use.
MaterialPicker.DeprecationMessage: Deprecated in favor of Material Manager. Don't use.

None.Summary: A rig type of None.

Inverse.Summary: Volume attenuates from Sound.RollOffMinDistance in an inverse manner, mirroring how sounds attenuate in the real world. This is done through Sound.RollOffMinDistance/distance, where distance is the Vector3.Magnitude between the audio source and the audio listener.

InverseTapered.Summary: A hybrid model which follows the Inverse model when close to Sound.RollOffMinDistance and the LinearSquare model when close to Sound.RollOffMaxDistance. This is done by taking the lesser of Inverse and LinearSquare.

Linear.Summary: Volume attenuates between Sound.RollOffMinDistance and Sound.RollOffMaxDistance with a linear relationship. This is done through (Sound.RollOffMaxDistance/distance)/(Sound.RollOffMaxDistance-Sound.RollOffMinDistance), where distance is the Vector3.Magnitude between the audio source and the audio listener.

LinearSquare.Summary: Volume attenuates between Sound.RollOffMinDistance and Sound.RollOffMaxDistance with a linear squared relationship. This is done through squaring Linear.

Legacy.Summary: Runs in legacy script containers dependent on the type of script uses such as LocalScript or Script.

Plugin.Summary: Runs as a descendant of Plugin instances.

FullscreenExtension.Summary:
If the total area of any descendant GuiObject within the ScreenGui (including any applied border or UIStroke) covers the device's safe area both horizontally and vertically, its background area will be expanded to cover the fullscreen area. This expansion does not affect the size or position of the descendant's content, except in the case of ImageLabel, ImageButton, or VideoFrame where the image/video is considered part of the background and will be expanded to fullscreen.

Note that this option is intended to automatically improve the appearance of UI that was authored for screens without any cutouts. However, it's recommended that you avoid fullscreen extensions for new work; instead, use the ScreenInsets property to specify which insets should be respected for different ScreenGuis.

None.Summary: Do not apply compatibility transformations to any descendants of the ScreenGui.

SaveAll.Summary: Saves all data, including both world and game-related information.

Crop.Summary: The image is cropped to fit within the element.

Fit.Summary: The image is scaled fit within the element X or Y dimension (whichever fits first).

Slice.Summary: 9-Slice scaling: slice the image into 9 regions and apply different scaling rules to each region. The slice boundaries are determined by ImageLabel.SliceCenter or ImageButton.SliceCenter. See UI 9-Slice Design for more information. .

Stretch.Summary: The image is stretched to fit within the element.

Tile.Summary: The image is tiled to fit within the element. For example, if the element is twice the X dimension of the image, the image will appear twice (2 tiles).

CoreUISafeInsets.Summary: Core UI insets are added to the DeviceSafeInsets area, resulting in an area guaranteed to be unobscured by both device screen cutouts and Roblox core UI elements like the top bar buttons. This mode is recommended for any ScreenGui that contains interactive and/or important UI elements such as buttons and status messages.

DeviceSafeInsets.Summary: Device safe area insets are added to the fullscreen area. The resulting area is guaranteed to not be occluded by any device screen cutouts such as the camera notch, although no inset is added for Roblox core UI elements like the top bar buttons. As a result, it's recommended that you use CoreUISafeInsets for a ScreenGui whose contents should remain unobscured by both device cutouts and core screen elements.

None.Summary: No insets are added to the fullscreen area. This mode may result in UI that is obscured or completely hidden by device notches and cutouts, so you should only use it for a ScreenGui that contains non‑interactive content like background images.

TopbarSafeInsets.Summary: Top bar safe area insets are added to the DeviceSafeInsets area, resulting in an area guaranteed to be unobscured by both device screen cutouts and Roblox core UI elements like the experience controls. Unlike CoreUISafeInsets, this area's position and size is dynamic and is limited to the space available within the top bar area itself, outside of CoreUISafeInsets.

LandscapeLeft.Summary: A preference where the game is displayed landscape (horizontally) with the bottom of the device on the left side of the screen.

LandscapeRight.Summary: A preference where the game is displayed landscape (horizontally) with the bottom of the device on the right side of the screen.

LandscapeSensor.Summary: A preference where the game is displayed landscape (horizontally) with the bottom of the device on the left of right side of the screen depending on the device's orientation (the sensor determines which side allows for the game to be displayed right-side-up).

Portrait.Summary: A preference where the game is displayed portrait (vertically) with the bottom of the device on the bottom of the screen.

Sensor.Summary: A preference where the game is displayed depending on the best match to the device's current orientation - either landscape (left/right) or portrait.

Always.Summary: The canvas will always be inset for the respective scroll bar, regardless of whether that scroll bar is showing.

None.Summary: The canvas will never be inset for the respective scroll bar.

ScrollBar.Summary: The canvas will only be inset if the respective scroll bar is showing.

X.Summary: The canvas can only be scrolled along the X axis.

XY.Summary: The canvas can be scrolled along both the X and Y axes.

Y.Summary: The canvas can only be scrolled along the Y axis.

Escape.Summary: Prioritizes GuiObjects within the same SelectionGroup but allows the selection to move to other outside GuiObjects if no suitable button is found.

BottomLeft.Summary: Bottom-left corner of the screen, with slight padding from the bottom and left edges.

BottomRight.Summary: Bottom-right corner of the screen, with slight padding from the bottom and right edges.

LastPosition.Summary: The position of the self view when it was last closed.

TopLeft.Summary: Top-left corner of the screen, with slight padding from the top and left edges.

TopRight.Summary: Top-right corner of the screen, with slight padding from the top and right edges.

AdAlreadyShowing.Summary: You are trying to show a full-screen ad while another full-screen ad is already playing.

AdNotReady.Summary: You are trying to show a full-screen ad before the ad has fully loaded. You might have failed to properly fetch the ad, or the ad might have expired.

InternalError.Summary: An unspecified internal error occurred. Try showing the ad again.

ShowCompleted.Summary: The ad was successfully shown to completion.

ShowInterrupted.Summary: The ad view of the user has been interrupted. The user might have closed the ad view or left the experience, and should not receive a reward.

AncestryDeferred.Summary: Equivalent to Deferred but only for events triggered by changes in ancestry.

Default.Summary: The default behavior; currently equivalent to Immediate but this will eventually change to Deferred.

Deferred.Summary: All events are deferred and their handlers resumed at specific resumptions points each frame.

Immediate.Summary: Event handlers are resumed immediately when the event occurs.

RelativeXX.Summary: The scale of X is shared with Y.

RelativeXY.Summary: The scale of X and Y are independent.

RelativeYY.Summary: The scale of Y is shared with X.

Custom.Summary: Elements are ordered by the function passed to UIGridStyleLayout:SetCustomSortFunction().

LayoutOrder.Summary: Elements are ordered by GuiObject.LayoutOrder in ascending order; for example 0 will be placed before 1.

Name.Summary: Elements are ordered by their Instance.Name in alphanumeric order.

Default.Summary: Currently equivalent to LowMemory. This will eventually change to Opportunistic.

LowMemory.Summary: Only stream out when memory is low.

Opportunistic.Summary: Stream out content that is significantly outside of the current StreamingRadius.

Default.Summary: Default behavior (currently equivalent to Disabled).

Disabled.Summary: Simulation of the replication focus is never paused, regardless of the amount of content streamed in on the client.

MinimumRadiusPause.Summary: All client-side simulation is paused when content is not streamed in up to the minimum radius.

PauseOutsideLoadedArea.Summary: Simulation of the replication focus is paused when any part of its bounding box is not in a streamed-in area.

Default.Summary: Default behavior (currently no change to gameplay).

Disabled.Summary: No change to gameplay due to streaming region availability.

Border.Summary: The color of borders, like those found in the Properties window.

ColorPickerFrame.Summary: The background color of the color picker.

Dropdown.Summary: The color of dropdown menus, like those found in the Properties window.

EmulatorBar.Summary: The color of the bar shown when the mobile emulator is active.

EmulatorDropDown.Summary: The color of the device and physical size dropdowns in the emulator bar.

GameSettingsTableItem.Summary: The color of items within tables in the settings window.

GameSettingsTooltip.Summary: The color of tooltips in the settings window.

InputFieldBackground.Summary: The background color of input fields, like those found in the Explorer window.

MainBackground.Summary: The primary background color used by the toolbar and windows.

MainButton.Summary: The background color of clickable buttons that are the primary action.

RibbonButton.Summary: The background color of buttons on the toolbar.

RibbonTab.Summary: The color of a tab on the toolbar menu.

ScrollBar.Summary: The color of scrollbar handles, like those seen in the Explorer window.

ScrollBarBackground.Summary: The background color of scrollbars, like those seen in the Explorer window.

Shadow.Summary: The color of shadows rendered under floating items like dropdowns.

StatusBar.Summary: The color of the status bar shown at the bottom of Studio, if it is visible.

Tab.Summary: The color of tabs on the tab bar, like the ones opened when the script editor is opened.

TabBar.Summary: The background color of the tab bar, like the one where the script editor is opened.

Tooltip.Summary: The background color of tooltips, like those seen when hovering over buttons on the toolbar or properties in the Properties window.

ViewPortBackground.Summary: The background color of the game viewport.

Paid.Summary: Payment for the subscription has been received.

Refunded.Summary: Payment for the subscription has been refunded.

NeverSubscribed.Summary: User has never subscribed to the product.

SubscribedRenewalPaymentPending.Summary: Subscription is active and renewal payment is pending.

SubscribedWillNotRenew.Summary: Subscription is active and will not renew.

Hinge.Summary: Makes the side appear with a yellow hinge. Any part connected to this hinge will stick to the side and rotate using physics.

Motor.Summary: Acts the same as a Hinge, but has a grey ring around it and automatically rotates any part connected to it.

None.Summary: No surface constraint.

SteppingMotor.Summary: Functions identically to a motor. It may have functioned differently in the past, but that functionality no longer seems to exist.

FixedSize.Summary: Renders with a fixed size set using SurfaceGui.CanvasSize.

PixelsPerStud.Summary: Renders with a variable size based on SurfaceGui.PixelsPerStud and the SurfaceGui's size in studs.

Hinge.Summary: Adds a yellow hinge to the surface. Parts touching it stick to the surface, allowing for rotations using physics. This should not be used for future work and existing instances should be replaced with a HingeConstraint.

Inlet.Summary: Adds square holes across the surface where studs would be.

Motor.Summary: Functioned identically to a hinge with the addition of a grey ring.

SmoothNoOutlines.Summary: Previously similar to Smooth with outlines but no longer relevant since outlines have been removed.

SteppingMotor.Summary: Functioned identically to a motor. It may have functioned differently in the past, but that functionality is non-existent.

Universal.Summary: Adds a checker pattern to the surface using studs and inlets.

None.Summary: The user did not swipe in a certain direction.

Compatibility.Summary: Simulates the removed legacy technology and is now deprecated. To achieve a similar look, use Voxel Lighting and add a ColorGradingEffect post‑processing effect set to the Retro preset.
Compatibility.DeprecationMessage: This option is deprecated and cannot be selected in Studio.

Future.Summary: Features the most advanced technology for high-fidelity lighting and shadows.

Legacy.DeprecationMessage: This option is deprecated and cannot be selected in Studio.

ShadowMap.Summary: Features shadow mapping that produces more realistic and crisp shadows from sunlight or directional light sources.

Unified.DeprecationMessage: This option is deprecated and cannot be selected in Studio.

Voxel.Summary: Uses a 4×4×4 voxel map for light and shadow calculation.

Failure.Summary: The teleport failed for an unknown reason.

Flooded.Summary: Too many teleport requests have been made recently.

GameEnded.Summary: The game that this player attempted to teleport to has ended.

GameFull.Summary: The game that this player attempted to teleport to is full.

GameNotFound.Summary: The game that this player attempted to teleport to could not be found.

Unauthorized.Summary: The player is not authorized to complete this teleport.

InProgress.Summary: The teleport is currently in progress. The player usually disconnects and teleports to the destination after this.

RequestedFromServer.Summary: The server has requested that the client teleport.

Started.Summary: The client has started attempting to teleport.

WaitingForServer.Summary: The client is waiting for the server to respond to the teleport request.

ToInstance.Summary: The teleport destination is an instance of a place.

ToPlace.Summary: The teleport destination is a place (no specific instance).

ToReservedServer.Summary: The destination of the teleport is a reserved server (a place instance that is reserved for a select group of players).

Floodchecked.Summary: Message is from a user sending messages too frequently.

InvalidPrivacySettings.Summary: Message can't be sent because of the user's chat privacy settings.

InvalidTextChannelPermissions.Summary: Message's TextSource is either not in the intended TextChannel or TextSource.CanSend is false.

TextFilterFailed.Summary: Text filter failed to process the message.

Unknown.Summary: Generic failed status for any other TextChannel:SendAsync() failures.

Text is truncated at the end of the text; extra graphemes that cannot fit into the space are replaced with .... Word boundaries are respected if possible.

For example, if the control is between -> and <- like so:

->Long text is truncated at the en<-d of the last complete word

The text will be:

None.Summary: Text is not truncated.

SplitWord.Summary:
If the end of the line occurs in the middle of a word, the text is truncated inside of that word. Extra graphemes that cannot fit into the space are replaced with ....

For example, if the control is between -> and <- like so:

->Long text is truncated at the en<-d of the last complete word

Center.Summary: Aligned starts at the center of the GUI object and spreads equally left and right.

Left.Summary: Alignment starts at the left side of the GUI object.

Right.Summary: Alignment starts at the right side of the GUI object.

Bottom.Summary: Alignment starts at the bottom of the GUI object.

Center.Summary: Aligned starts at the center of the GUI object and spreads equally toward the top and bottom.

Top.Summary: Alignment starts at the top of the GUI object.

Static.Summary:
For a Trail, the texture will be rolled out as the attachments move, and they will remain in place until their lifetime is met. This setting is ideal for trail textures that should appear "stamped" where rendered, such as paw prints or tire tracks.

This value is not supported for Beam and therefore behaves identically to Wrap.

Stretch.Summary:
For a Trail, the texture will stretch out based on the lifetime of the trail, and shrink inwards if the trail's attachments stop moving.

For a Beam, the texture will repeat TextureLength times across the beam's overall length. See here for details.

Wrap.Summary:
For a Trail, the texture will be tiled as the length of the trail changes, but the textures will remain stationary relative to their attachments.

For a Beam, the texture repetitions will equal the beam's overall length (in studs) divided by its TextureLength. See here for details.

NonHumanoidOrphaned.Summary: Unreferenced texture memory for objects other than Humanoid.

Auto.Summary: Let task scheduler make a decision internally.

PerCore1.Summary: Utilize 1 worker thread per available physical CPU core.

PerCore2.Summary: Utilize 2 worker threads per available physical CPU core.

PerCore3.Summary: Utilize 3 worker threads per available physical CPU core.

PerCore4.Summary: Utilize 4 worker threads per available physical CPU core.

Threads1.Summary: Utilize 1 worker thread, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Threads16.Summary: Utilize 16 worker threads, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Threads2.Summary: Utilize 2 worker threads, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Threads3.Summary: Utilize 3 worker threads, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Threads4.Summary: Utilize 4 worker threads, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Threads8.Summary: Utilize 8 worker threads, ignore the physical CPU core count.

Default.Summary: Standard throttling.

AvatarBust.Summary: The returned thumbnail shows the bust (chest up) of the user's avatar.

AvatarThumbnail.Summary: The returned thumbnail shows the entire body of the user's avatar.

HeadShot.Summary: The returned thumbnail shows just the headshot (head and up) of the user's avatar.

Benchmark.Summary: Dynamically decide between using ''Fast'' and ''Precise'' depending on performance.

Fast.Summary: Compute time using a faster, but less precise method.

Default.Summary: Sets the tone mapper to use the post‑2019 Roblox appearance which provides vivid colors and high contrasts.

Retro.Summary: Sets the tone mapper to imitate the pre‑2019 Roblox appearance. Colors look less saturated and there is less contrast between them.

Center.Summary: The object is centered around the center of its parent.

Classic.Summary: Default mode used by Roblox core scripts.

Default.Summary: Default mode used by Roblox core scripts.

Follow.Summary: Camera moves with the subject and rotates to keep the subject in the center.

Orbital.Summary: The camera locks at a certain angle. Once it's set, players can rotate the camera, but it will always maintain a consistent angle to the ground.

ClickToMove.Summary: Change the movement controller to click to move.

DPad.Summary: Change the movement controller to the DPad.

Default.Summary: The default movement controller.

DynamicThumbstick.Summary: Change the movement controller to the dynamic thumbstick.

Thumbpad.Summary: Change the movement controller to the thumbpad.

Thumbstick.Summary: Change the movement controller to the classic thumbstick.

Automatic.Summary: Mimics EntireObject behavior for a UI object that's entirely contained by the BoundingUI, or else HitPoint for a UI object that's partially outside the BoundingUI.

EntireObject.Summary: Bounds the entire dragged UI object within the BoundingUI.

HitPoint.Summary: Bounds the dragged UI only by the exact hit/grab point and its respective position after translation/rotation.

Absolute.Summary: Designates the input and return values as the absolute target position/rotation in the space defined by DragSpace.

Relative.Summary: Designates the input and return values as the change from the current position/rotation in the space defined by DragSpace.

LayerCollector.Summary: Designates the input and return values' space as that of the LayerCollector.

Parent.Summary: Designates the input and return values' space as the local space of the detector's parent GuiObject.

Reference.Summary:
Designates the input and return values' space as that of the ReferenceUIInstance. For DragRelativity and DragUDim2 purposes, the (0, 0) origin is the absolute center position of the ReferenceUIInstance.

If ReferenceUIInstance is not nil, this will behave the same as Parent.

Rotate.Summary: By default, rotation about the absolute center position of the detector's parent GuiObject. If ReferenceUIInstance is set, rotation happens about that instance's absolute center position.

Scriptable.Summary: Calculates desired motion via a custom function provided through SetDragStyleFunction().

TranslatePlane.Summary: 2D motion in the plane of the LayerCollector.

CustomOffset.Summary: The UI element will not move at all, but the Offset values of the detector's DragUDim2 will still be updated and the detector's events will still fire, allowing you to respond to drag manipulation however you'd like.

CustomScale.Summary: The UI element will not move at all, but the Scale values of the detector's DragUDim2 will still be updated and the detector's events will still fire, allowing you to respond to drag manipulation however you'd like.

Offset.Summary: Move by the Offset values of the detector's parent's GuiObject.Position value.

Scale.Summary: Move by the Scale values of the detector's parent's GuiObject.Position value.

XX.Summary: Both the X and Y axis speeds are based off the X axis for Scale, while the Offset values still apply to their respective axis.

XY.Summary: Default setting for a detector's UIDragSpeedAxisMapping where the X and Y axis speeds are based off the X and Y Scale/Offset values respectively.

YY.Summary: Both the X and Y axis speeds are based off the Y axis for Scale, while the Offset values still apply to their respective axis.

Fill.Summary: Siblings resize to fill the entire parent container, overriding their defined width or height.

None.Summary: No flex behavior; siblings maintain their defined width or height.

SpaceAround.Summary: Siblings maintain their defined width or height. Equal spacing is added on both sides of each sibling.

SpaceBetween.Summary: Siblings maintain their defined width or height. Equal spacing is added between siblings, but no additional space is added around siblings.

SpaceEvenly.Summary: Siblings maintain their defined width or height. Equal spacing is added both between and around siblings.

Custom.Summary: Enables the GrowRatio and ShrinkRatio properties for the UIFlexItem, allowing for relative growth or shrinking of the parent GuiObject in a ratio compared to other flex objects also under control of a UIFlexItem.

Fill.Summary: Sets an effective 1:1 grow‑shrink ratio on the parent GuiObject. This setting ensures the flex line always fills the container, even if the container size changes.

Grow.Summary: Sets an effective 1:0 grow‑shrink ratio on the parent GuiObject. Objects set to Grow never shrink below their basis size, so overflow may occur if the container becomes smaller than the flex line's combined basis size.

None.Summary: The parent GuiObject is unaffected and neither shrinks nor grows.

Shrink.Summary: Sets an effective 0:1 grow‑shrink ratio on the parent GuiObject. Objects set to Shrink never grow above their basis size, so underflow may occur if the container becomes larger than the flex line's combined basis size.

LeftHand.Summary: The CFrame of the user's left hand.

RightHand.Summary: The CFrame of the user's right hand.

Begin.Summary: Occurs when an InputObject starts to interact with the experience. For example, a mouse button down, a key down, or when the player begins touching the screen.

Cancel.Summary: A special circumstance state that indicates this input is no longer relevant, particularly with ContextActionService. For example, binding two action-handling functions will cause the first to Cancel if an input was already in-progress when the second was bound.

Change.Summary: Occurs each frame an InputObject has already begun interacting with the experience and part of its state is changing. For example, movement of the mouse position, a gamepad thumbstick movement, an analog gamepad trigger button change, or screen touch point change.

End.Summary: Occurs when an InputObject finishes interacting with the experience. For example, a mouse button up, a key up, or when the player stops touching the screen.

None.Summary: A state that should never be seen in an experience; essentially just marks the end of the enum.

Focus.Summary: The client regaining focus of the Roblox window.

InputMethod.Summary: Text input from an input method editor (IME). InputObjects with this type aren't currently fired.

MouseMovement.Summary: Movement of the mouse. Fires changed events each time the player's cursor position changes and when the move enters/leaves the game window.

None.Summary: Unknown UserInputType.

TextInput.Summary: Input of Text into a text-based GuiObject. Normally this is only a TextBox.

Touch.Summary: A tap on the screen from a mobile device.

World.Summary: Adjusts `Class.Camera.HeadScale' so that the world in VR is seen from the avatar's perspective.

ABXY.Summary: The touchpad will function as a means of inputting the standard ABXY gamepad input, dividing it up into 4 diagonal pie slices.

Touch.Summary: The touchpad is treated as ButtonB if it is the left touchpad, or ButtonA if it is the right touchpad.

VirtualThumbstick.Summary: The touchpad will function as a gamepad joystick.

Line.Summary:
The velocity component in the direction of the line is constrained to the specified value. The line direction is based on the RelativeTo property:

  • Attachment0 - The line direction is the primary axis of Attachment0.
  • Attachment1 - The line direction is the primary axis of Attachment1.
  • World - The line direction must be specified.

Plane.Summary:
The velocity components in the plane are constrained to the specified values. The plane tangents are based on the RelativeTo property:

  • Attachment0 - The plane tangents are the two axes of Attachment0.
  • Attachment1 - The plane tangents are the two axes of Attachment1.
  • World - The two plane tangents must be specified

Vector.Summary:
The velocity components must be equal to the vector components specified. The coordinate system of the vector is based on the RelativeTo property:

  • Attachment0 - The vector components are in the coordinate system defined by the axes of Attachment0.
  • Attachment1 - The vector components are in the coordinate system defined by the axes of Attachment1.
  • World - The coordinate system is in the world and the vector components must be specified.

Bottom.Summary: Grid is aligned to the bottom edge of its parent.

Center.Summary: Grid is aligned to the center of its parent along the Y axis.

Top.Summary: Grid is aligned to the top edge of its parent.

Default.Summary: The Virtual Cursor is in the default state.

Enabled.Summary: The Virtual Cursor is enabled.

Inverse.Summary: Represents a distance attenuation curve that follows the inverse-squared law. This is identical to the default distance attenuation of an AudioEmitter instance.

Legacy.Summary: Represents a linear-squared distance attenuation curve with a minimum distance of 7 and a maximum distance of 80. This is identical to the distance attenuation used in the internal-only default voice setup that does not use AudioDeviceInput and AudioEmitter objects.

All.Summary: All WeldConstraints will be returned in the recommended table.

None.Summary: WeldConstraints will be ignored and not returned in the recommended table.

Touching.Summary: Only WeldConstraints that connect touching parts in the performed operation will be returned in the recommended table.

BoundCage.Summary: This debug mode visualizes corresponding cage mesh vertices bound to an underlying WrapTarget. In order to find corresponding vertices between different cages, the Wrap Deformer algorithm uses UV matching. As long as your WrapLayer cage mesh share the same UV layout as WrapTarget, its vertices will be marked as "bound".

BoundCageAndLinks.Summary: The same as BoundCage but also visualizes how bound vertices were moved. You can use this mode to identify where they belong on a previous layer and where they are located on the current layer.

LayerCage.Summary: This debug mode shows the resulting layer mesh as a whole. The deformer will use vertex locations from the previous layer for all unbound vertices.

None.Summary: This debug rendering mode does nothing. This is the default value.

OuterCage.Summary: This debug mode shows the original outer cage mesh as it was created.

Rbf.Summary: This debug mode visualizes the internal RBF solver state. You can estimate the wrap deformer's expected behavior by looking at this state. All renderable mesh vertices move from a "big sphere" to a "small sphere" along a corresponding line connecting two spheres.

Reference.Summary: This debug mode shows the original inner cage mesh as it was created.

None.Summary: This debug rendering mode does nothing, and this is the default value.

Rbf.Summary: This debug mode visualizes the internal RBF solver state. You can estimate the wrap deformer expected behavior by looking at this state. All renderable mesh vertices move from a "big sphere" to a "small sphere" along a corresponding line connecting two spheres.

TargetCageCompressed.Summary: This debug mode shows corresponding cage mesh compressed by clothing layers above it. This debug mode is intended to validate that the compression algorithm and corresponding cages work as intended.

TargetCageInterface.Summary: This debug mode shows the resulting cage mesh for the corresponding Wrap Instance. This debug mode is intended to validate that the final deformed cage looks as intended.

TargetCageOriginal.Summary: This debug mode shows the original cage mesh as it was created.

TargetLayerCageCompressed.Summary: The same as TargetCageCompressed but affects all WrapTargets that belong to the Wrap Deformer simultaneously. It doesn't matter which particular WrapTarget you enable this debug visualization option.

TargetLayerCageOriginal.Summary: The same as TargetCageOriginal but affects all WrapTargets that belong to the Wrap Deformer simultaneously. It doesn't matter which particular WrapTarget you enable this debug visualization option.

TargetLayerInterface.Summary: The same as TargetCageInterface but affects all WrapTargets that belong to the Wrap Deformer simultaneously. It doesn't matter which particular WrapTarget you enable this debug visualization option.

Global.Summary: The ZIndex property overrides the default value computed from the depth in the hierarchy.

Sibling.Summary: The ZIndex property controls the order in which the GuiObject renders relative to its siblings.

BrickColor.Summary: A data type that provides a predefined list of named colors.
BrickColor.Description:
The BrickColor data type provides a predefined list of named colors, not to be confused with Color3, a more general data type that describes RGB colors. The following code shows how to use BrickColor.new() to declare the BrickColor property of a Part.

local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

-- By color name
Workspace.Part.BrickColor = BrickColor.new("Pastel Blue")
-- By numerical index
Workspace.Part.BrickColor = BrickColor.new(11)
-- By RGB decimal values in range of 0-1
Workspace.Part.BrickColor = BrickColor.new(0.502, 0.734, 0.859)

Constructors.Name: new
Constructors.Summary: Returns a CFrame with the position of the first Vector3 and an orientation pointed toward the second.
Constructors.Description:
Returns a new CFrame located at pos and facing towards lookAt, assuming that (0, 1, 0) is considered "up" in world space.

This constructor overload has been replaced by CFrame.lookAt(), which accomplishes a similar goal. It remains for the sake of backward compatibility.

At high pitch angles (around 82 degrees), you may experience numerical instability. If this is an issue, or if you require a different "up" vector, use CFrame.fromMatrix() to more accurately construct the CFrame. Additionally, if lookAt is directly above pos (pitch angle of 90 degrees), the "up" vector switches to the X axis.

CFrame.Summary: A data type that represents both a 3D position and orientation.
CFrame.Description:
The CFrame data type, short for coordinate frame, describes a 3D position and orientation. It is made up of a positional component and a rotational component and includes essential arithmetic operations for working with 3D data on Roblox.

1
2

-- Create a CFrame at a certain position and Euler rotation
local cf = CFrame.new(0, 5, 0) * CFrame.fromEulerAngles(math.rad(45), 0, 0)

For an introduction to the CFrame data type, see CFrames.

Positional Component

The positional component is available as a Vector3. In addition, the components of a CFrame object's position are also available in the X, Y and Z properties like a Vector3.

Rotational Component

CFrame stores 3D rotation data in a 3×3 rotation matrix. These values are returned by the CFrame:GetComponents() function after the x, y and z positional values. This matrix is used internally when doing calculations involving rotations, using radians as their unit (for conversion from one to the other, use math.rad() or math.deg()). For more information on how the Roblox Engine performs rotations, see RotationOrder.

The table below represents the components of a CFrame object's rotation matrix and their relationship with the available vector properties such as LookVector and RightVector. Although the individual components of the rotation matrix are rarely useful by themselves, the vector properties which derive from them are much more useful.

XVector, RightVector YVector, UpVector ZVector, -LookVector†
R00 R01 R02
R10 R11 R12
R20 R21 R22

ColorSequence.Summary: A gradient of color values comprised of ColorSequenceKeypoints.
ColorSequence.Description:
The ColorSequence data type represents a gradient of color values from 0 to 1. The color values are expressed using the ColorSequenceKeypoint type. This type is used in various properties of ParticleEmitter, Trail, Beam, and other objects that use color gradients.

Equality

Two ColorSequence objects are equivalent only if the values of their ColorSequenceKeypoint are equivalent, even if both would result in similar gradients.

Evaluation

The ColorSequence type does not have a built-in method for getting the value at a certain time/point. However, you can use the following function to evaluate at a specific time.

local function evalColorSequence(sequence: ColorSequence, time: number)
    -- If time is 0 or 1, return the first or last value respectively
    if time == 0 then
        return sequence.Keypoints[1].Value
    elseif time == 1 then
        return sequence.Keypoints[#sequence.Keypoints].Value
    end

    -- Otherwise, step through each sequential pair of keypoints
    for i = 1, #sequence.Keypoints - 1 do
        local thisKeypoint = sequence.Keypoints[i]
        local nextKeypoint = sequence.Keypoints[i + 1]
        if time >= thisKeypoint.Time and time < nextKeypoint.Time then
            -- Calculate how far alpha lies between the points
            local alpha = (time - thisKeypoint.Time) / (nextKeypoint.Time - thisKeypoint.Time)
            -- Evaluate the real value between the points using alpha
            return Color3.new(
                (nextKeypoint.Value.R - thisKeypoint.Value.R) * alpha + thisKeypoint.Value.R,
                (nextKeypoint.Value.G - thisKeypoint.Value.G) * alpha + thisKeypoint.Value.G,
                (nextKeypoint.Value.B - thisKeypoint.Value.B) * alpha + thisKeypoint.Value.B
            )
        end
    end
end

Returns a new DateTime representing the current moment in time, using the device's local clock. Constructors.Name: fromUniversalTime
Constructors.Summary: Returns a new DateTime using the given units from a UTC time.
Constructors.Description:
Returns a new DateTime using the given units from a UTC time. The values accepted are similar to those found in the time value table returned by ToUniversalTime().

  • Date units (year, month, day) that produce an invalid date will raise an error. For example, January 32nd or February 29th on a non-leap year.
  • Time units (hour, minute, second, millisecond) that are outside their normal range are valid. For example, 90 minutes will cause the hour to roll over by 1; -10 seconds will cause the minute value to roll back by 1.
  • Non-integer values are rounded down. For example, providing 2.5 hours will be equivalent to providing 2 hours, not 2 hours 30 minutes.
  • Omitted values are assumed to be their lowest value in their normal range, except for year which defaults to 1970.
